name: How long does a sewer line replacement take?

mainEntity.name: How long does a sewer line replacement take?

acceptedAnswer.text: The duration of a sewer line replacement varies based on the complexity of the project and the method chosen. A straightforward traditional trenching replacement for a residential property might take 1 to 3 days, depending on soil conditions and pipe length. Trenchless methods, such as pipe bursting or lining, can sometimes be completed in 1 to 2 days, as they require less excavation. Factors like permit acquisition, weather conditions, and unexpected complications can also influence the total timeline. We will provide an estimated timeframe during your consultation.
acceptedAnswer.description: Sewer line replacement can take 1 to 3 days for traditional methods or 1 to 2 days for trenchless, depending on project complexity and conditions.
